thread.title_full: Judge disqualifies accused sexual offender's attorney; cites potential conflict of interest - NewsBreak

author: Bill O Boyle
title: Judge disqualifies accused sexual offender's attorney; cites potential conflict of interest - NewsBreak
text:
By Bill O Boyle [email protected] ,
16 hours ago WILKES-BARRE — Citing the potential for a conflict of interest in the case against Richard Garnett, who is accused of sexually assaulting a boy during Bible study classes, Luzerne County Judge Joseph Sklarosky Jr. disqualified the defendant’s attorney on Wednesday.
Judge Sklarosky ruled that because Attorney George Gossett had previously represented another suspect in the case, he could have information that could constitute a conflict of interest in Garnett’s trial.
Judge Sklarosky qualified his ruling, stating that he in no way was casting any aspersions toward Gossett as an attorney, rather explaining that any conflict of interest could result in a mistrial.
“The best way I can put it is that I don’t know what you know,” Judge Sklarosky said. “Therefore, should we proceed and a conflict does arise, we could end up with a mistrial and be right back here again.”
Gossett told the judge that his prior representation of Pastor Dan Brubaker of the Roaring Brook Baptist Church in Hunlock Township, has always been known, but the issue was never brought up until now.
Brubaker was in the courtroom with his current attorney, Ryan Blazure. Sklarosky asked Brubaker to come forward with his attorney. Brubaker said he had no objection to his former attorney (Gossett) representing Garnett.
Judge Sklarosky noted that Brubaker has been subpoenaed to testify for the Commonwealth at trial.
Garnett told the judge that he preferred to keep Gossett as his attorney, but Sklarosky decided to disqualify him.
An assistant Luzerne County Public Defender, Nathan Hartman, was in the courtroom and said he would likely be assigned to defend Garnett, providing the defendant does not seek private counsel.
The case was continued for 30 days to allow for new counsel to prepare.
The Commonwealth is represented by Chief Deputy Attorney General Angela Sperrazza and Deputy Attorney General Mamie Phillips.
Case background
In December 2024 , the Pennsylvania Superior Court reversed a ruling by Judge Sklarosky, who denied prosecutors the use of Garnett’s convictions on child sex offenses.
Garnett is accused by the Pennsylvania State Police at Wilkes-Barre with sexually assaulting a boy during Bible study classes at Roaring Brook Baptist Church between 2004 and 2006 , according to court records.
The boy came forward with the allegations in 2017, and shortly after, investigators served a search warrant at the church on Dec. 6, 2017, seizing computers and documents listing attendance records of students and teachers. Garnett was a volunteer at the church during the time of the alleged offenses.
Before the search warrant was executed, the boy identified another person who allegedly assaulted him at the Baptist church.
During a separate investigation by state police that involved Garnett being accused of sexually assaulting two girls inside private homes between 1980 and 1984, investigators discovered the boy mistakenly identified the man who allegedly sexually assaulted him inside the church.
Garnett pleaded guilty to two counts of involuntary deviate sexual intercourse in reference to the sexual offenses against the two girls, and was sentenced by Judge Sklarosky in June 2021, to 6-16 years in state prison.
As Garnett faces charges of statutory sexual assault, involuntary deviate sexual intercourse, endangering the welfare of children, indecent assault, and corruption of minors regarding the boy, Pennsylvania Deputy Attorney General Susan E. Affronti was denied by Sklarosky to use Garnett’s convictions for sexually assaulting the girls.
On appeal, a three-member panel of the Superior Court overturned Sklarosky’s refusal, ultimately permitting prosecutors to use Garnett’s prior convictions against him during the open case of sexually abusing the boy.
The appellate court sent Garnett’s case back to Sklarosky for further proceedings.
